title: Transformation
idea:
Hypothesis: our winning skin tag angle (#316) will work in our winning UGC format (#107), with her real before and after on screen from the first frame.
WHY: #107 is our winning UGC format (one woman filming her routine, her voice over it; $28.2k spent). #316's angle (skin tags gone without the pain, blood and scar of the other methods) took 27% of last week's spend. We have never put the two together.
WHAT: a short UGC review in the #107 format, selling the #316 angle, with her real before and after on screen from the first frame.
HOW: one woman, one movement (rolling it on her neck), her own voiceover. 3 hooks that change only the on-screen text.

I have to show you guys this.
I've had this little skin tag on my neck for years, and it kept getting caught on my necklace. It drove me crazy.
I wanted to get rid of it, but I wasn't about to cut it off or freeze it and risk bleeding or ending up with a scar. Not over something this tiny.
So I started looking for something I could try at home, and I came across this castor oil roller from Haven & Spool.
I started rolling it on every night before bed. Ten seconds, right on the spot.
A few weeks in, I looked in the mirror one morning, and it was just... gone. I didn't even feel it come off.
Look. Same spot.
I'll leave the link below if you wanna try it.

Avatar: Women 45–65 in the US with a skin tag on the neck that bothers them every day (catches on necklaces and collars, shows in photos).
Desire: get rid of it without cutting, freezing, bleeding or a scar.
Behavior: they know the usual fixes (cutting it off, freezing it, the dermatologist) and have put them off, out of fear of the pain or the scar, or because it felt too small to pay a doctor for.
Belief: the only real ways to remove it hurt or leave a mark.
Awareness: solution aware.
